positions.title: Dynamics CRM Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
CRM Lead Developer for eApp Grant Management App

Client: Office of Statewide Health Planning and Development (OSHPD) 

OSHPD was seeking a replacement for its former health grant system by leveraging Microsoft Dynamics CRM. The new grant management system, eApp, supports the application, eligibility determination, and funding source management for over 20 grant programs administered by OSHPD to thousands of healthcare professionals. It allows users to submit applications and store supplemental documents via Sharepoint.

My role and responsibilities as a CRM Lead Developer was to architect a Grants Management solution that could host multiple unique application processes, capture applicant data through a public-facing portal, evaluate eligible applicants, and execute grant payments for awardees. Developed C# business rule plugin workflow library, JavaScript/jQuery libraries for Front-End portal enhancement, and CRM customizations for data hierarchy modeling and lifecycle stages.

Notable Achievements: 
- Geo API integration library for automated Address Validation
- Microsoft Portal bulk-upload solution to give portal users the ability to batch-upload applicant data
- Sharepoint Document integration library for storing, validating, and managing applicant documents.
- SRSS Reporting integration for portal-user access to CRM reports.
- Successful CRM and Portal Deployment of the OSHPD Funding eApp service

Technology: Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2016 On-Prem, Adxstudio Portals 7.0, SharePoint 2013, SSRS Reporting Services

projects.title: Haar Face Detection Acceleration in Hardware
projects.description: Our group was tasked by Altera to examine one of the Face Detection algorithms in the OpenCV Library and attempt to accelerate the function in Hardware on a Cyclone IV FPGA board. My role in this project was to analyze the C++ code for the Viola Jones Object Detection Framework, visually represent the function tree and the flow of the algorithm, and create a Verilog design that can be implemented into Programmable Logic.

projects.title: Zedboard Interrupt Latency Analysis
projects.description: Our group was tasked by Xilinx to test the interrupt performance of the ARM processors on an SoC Development board, the Zedboard. We tested the Zedboard's interrupt performance in both its embedded processor mode and its embedded Linux mode. For testing the Interrupt Latency in embedded processor mode, we instantiated an AXI Timer IP module on the Programmable Logic side, and then wrote a user application in C on the Programmable System side that will communicate with the AXI Timer. For testing the Interrupt Latency in embedded Linux mode, we wrote a Device Driver for the AXI Timer and a user application that will invoke the drive and issue commands to the AXI Timer Module. My role for this project was to manage the Programmable Logic side of the Zedboard, properly instantiate the AXI Timer module on the board, and solely be responsible for writing the firmware and device driver code that interacts with the AXI Timer.
